title: Dynamic onboarding paths with questionnaire slicing and insurance crediting pilot
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background:
Redwood frequently stalls during enterprise vendor onboarding because the standard security questionnaire is all-or-nothing: any vendor that indicates a single production data access path gets routed to a 40+ question SOC2-full flow, which adds 2–4 weeks to procurement. Meanwhile, larger customers expect pricing concessions or insurance offsets for dedicated capacity or private deployments.

Problem statement:
- Onboarding time for vendors and partners (including marketplace & channel partners) is high when the intake flow forces a full questionnaire for low-risk vendors.
- Procurement teams want a predictable, contract+insurance-first path that reduces negotiation friction for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Current process lacks an automated link between questionnaire outcome (risk tranche) and pricing/insurance crediting offers.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a dynamic onboarding path that "slices" the security questionnaire into a lightweight SOC2-lite path and a full SOC2-required path based on automated gating logic. Pair this with a pricing/insurance crediting experiment that offers conditional credits or contract templates for vendors who provide verifiable evidence (attestations, insurance certificates, signed ATO artifacts).

Key features to deliver:
1) Questionnaire slicing ruleset: a small rules engine run at intake (jurisdiction, data categories, infra access, role-based access, customer-controlled keys) that assigns a temporary risk tranche (low/medium/high). Low-tranche vendors receive SOC2-lite (15 questions + targeted evidence requests).
2) Evidence stitching & attestations: support for signed attestations (PDF + e-sign), hosted evidence links, and automated verification of insurance COI (Certificate of Insurance) metadata.
3) Pricing & insurance crediting flow: map risk tranche to a set of contract recommendations and a standard crediting offer (e.g., pre-approved 3% credit for vendors with valid COI / SOC2-lite + 3rd-party attestation). This integrates with Sales comp/pricing playbooks.
4) Contract templates & e-sign integration: pre-filled master services addendum with indemnity and SLA clauses according to tranche, plus DocuSign e-sign link generation.
5) Console signals & dashboards: surface time-to-onboard, accepted credits, and rejection reasons to procurement and account teams.

Acceptance criteria (must-haves):
- Intake form routes >80% of non-sensitive vendors to SOC2-lite correctly in pilot data (manual audit sample of 100 intake forms).
- Automated COI parsing successfully extracts insurer name, effective/expiry dates, and limits for >=90% of submitted PDFs in the pilot.
- Pricing credit workflow auto-generates a contract addendum and credit recommendation for Sales in >95% of accepted cases.
- Legal signs off on SOC2-lite evidence bundle and contract templates for pilot customers.

Success metrics (primary):
- Time-to-onboard (median) reduced from ~14 days to <=5 days for vendors that qualify for SOC2-lite.
- Number of procurement cycles closed with auto crediting >= 15 pilot pilots in quarter.
- Percentage of Dedicated/Private deals where insurance credit led to faster signature >= 20% improvement vs baseline.

Implementation plan & milestones:
- Week 1: Finalize ruleset and gating decisions with Security/Legal (deliverable: rules doc).
- Week 2–3: Build intake changes + evidence collection API (ENG-4821).
- Week 4: COI parsing prototype and attestation upload + e-sign link plumbing (integration work with Solutions Eng).
- Week 5: Contract template generation + sales UI in procurement console.
- Week 6: Pilot with 3 sales accounts and collect metrics; iterate.

Open trade-offs / design notes:
- Conservative gating reduces risk but reduces value of the experiment; we’ll bias toward recall (i.e., prefer safety) on initial rollout and tune after pilot.
- Automated COI parsing may misclassify non-standard PDFs; we will fallback to a human-in-the-loop reviewer in the console.
- Credits vs discounts decision: credits are easier to operationalize for short pilots since they can be applied as bill credits post-signature; discounts require longer-term billing changes.

Stakeholders & reviewers:

- Sales/RevOps: Elena Park (pricing experiments)
- Eng: Backend lead (ENG-4821), Console lead (ENG-4999)

Rollout approach:
- Alpha pilot with 3 existing procurement leads (Finance + Platform teams) who consent to expedited ruleset testing.
- Evaluate on 30–90 day lead sample and iterate ruleset thresholds and evidence requirements.
- If pilot meets acceptance criteria, roll to beta for all Deals > $50k ARR, gate via feature flag.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: False negatives routing sensitive vendors to SOC2-lite. Mitigation: conservative initial ruleset and automated sampling with daily security reviews.
- Risk: Insurance credit abuse. Mitigation: validate COI metadata and tie credit issuance to signed contract and post-signature audit.
- Risk: Legal rejection of standardized indemnity language. Mitigation: involve Legal early and add clause toggles per geography.
